'''Carole Baker Lacampagne'''  (12 September 1933 – 5 August 2021)<ref>{{cite journal
|date        = January 2022
|title       = Community Updates
|url         = https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/202201/rnoti-p131.pdf
|journal     = Notices of the American Mathematical Society
|volume      = 69
|issue       = 1
|pages       = 134
|doi         = 
|access-date = 21 May 2025
}}</ref> was an American mathematician. She is known for her work in [[mathematics education]] and [[gender equality]].<ref name=handbook>''Contributors'' (2007). In S. S. Klein (Ed.), Handbook for achieving gender equity through education (2nd Ed.) (pp 359-380). Mahwah, NJ: Lawrence Erlbaum.p. xiii</ref>

==Career==
Lacampagne received her Ed.D. from [[Teachers College, Columbia University]] in 1979.<ref>{{cite web|title=A Closer Look at Women's Colleges, Appendix|url=http://www2.ed.gov/pubs/WomensColleges/appendix.html|location=US Department of Education}}</ref> She then worked at [[Northern Illinois University]] and the [[National Science Foundation]] before moving to the Department of Education in 1991, becoming Director of the National Institute on Postsecondary Education, Libraries, and Lifelong Learning (PLLI). She then became Director of the Mathematical Sciences Education Board at the [[National Academies of Science]] before her partial retirement as an adjunct at [[George Washington University]].<ref name=handbook />

==Work for gender equality==
Lacampagne was actively involved in supporting women in mathematics, and became head of the Women and Mathematic's program of the [[Mathematical Association of America]].<ref name=handbook/> She wrote about women and mathematics throughout her career, including her 1979 dissertation.<ref>{{cite thesis|title=An evaluation of the Women and Mathematics (WAM) program and associated sex-related differences in the teaching, learning, and counseling of mathematics|year=1979|first=Carole Baker|last=Campagne|type=Ed.D.|publisher=[[Teachers College, Columbia University]]}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==

In 2012, Lacampagne became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society |access-date=2015-02-06 |archive-date=2018-08-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Selected publications==
*Lacampagne, Carole B., et al. "Gender equity in mathematics." Handbook for achieving gender equity through education (2007): 235–253.
*Lacampagne, Carole B. State of the Art: Transforming Ideas for Teaching and Learning Mathematics. US Dept. of Education, OERI Education Information, 555 New Jersey Avenue, NW, Washington, DC 20208-5641
